findings.summary: The docs summary can imply that the second due check stops the lane even when a young command defers the sequence.
evidence: docs/agent-task-runs.md says “a second due check, deferred while a young command runs, stops it.”
The spec says that when a young command defers the request at a due check, the next empty due check delivers the request, and the stop waits one more check. That next check does not stop the lane.
findings.action: Clarify that the second empty due check stops only when the request was already delivered; when a young command defers the sequence, the next due check delivers the request and a later empty check stops.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-003: snapshot work can delay later checks, so a hard wall-clock bound is not established.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The spec names the live snapshot as work that delays the next check and explicitly states that windows are nominal and it gives no hard wall-clock bound.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-004: release notes and docstring still describe a fixed extra window.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes say deferral is by one more check and explain that windows are nominal; the docstring also says deferral is by one check and that windows are nominal.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-004: docs summary describes stop timing under young-command deferral.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The summary’s second-due-check wording is ambiguous in a way that can lead readers to expect a stop before the request is delivered.

next_move: Clarify the docs summary’s due-check sequence, then repeat the bounded review.
non_claims: Reviewed the identity-bound inline payload; did not inspect workspace paths or run tests.
Did not independently verify unrelated release-note claims.
